results.summary: This project implements a hardware-accelerated Cooley-Tukey Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) butterfly core optimized for CRYSTALS-Kyber post-quantum cryptography with q = 3329. It performs fast modular addition and subtraction using specialized combinational subtraction matrix logic blocks without slow division operations. The design provides X_out and Y_out buses for the butterfly results, with A_in and B_in input buses and split bidirectional lines for B_in and Y_out. Testing is done by applying input arrays and twiddle factors, then driving clock transitions to observe the modular transformation outputs.

results.summary_before: This project implements a neural network encoder that loads a 6-bit input and shifts it out while encoding the bits for display. The write_not_shift control selects between loading and shifting, and the encoded bits are shown one at a time on an 8-segment display. It is tested using the standard Tiny Tapeout board with DIP switches and a display. The design demonstrates neural network encoding and shift register operation.
results.summary: This project implements a very simple 7-segment cellular automaton using about 200 basic logic gates. At each clock cycle, each of the seven segments is set alive or dead based on whether it had exactly one living neighbor when alive or exactly two living neighbors when dead, where touching segments are neighbors. Seven flip-flops hold the state, combinatorial logic computes the next state, and the state is latched on a clock edge; support logic allows manual loading, clock division, and run mode. It is tested on the standard Tiny Tapeout PCB using DIP switches for control and the seven-segment display for output, with additional puzzles suggested for the reader.

results.summary_before: This project generates an I2S bit clock by counting system clock cycles and producing a divided clock signal. It is used with an I2S audio interface, and the clock frequency is determined by the count value. The design includes a counter and a clock divider. It is notable for its role in audio clock generation.
results.summary: This project converts SPDIF audio to I2S format for a ClassD amplifier MA12070p. It oversamples the SPDIF input using a 27 MHz system clock, regenerates the I2S bit clock by counting system clock cycles between SPDIF edges, and detects left/right sync words to toggle the I2S word-select signal. PCM samples are decoded from phase/mark changes, shifted into left and right FIFOs, and output on i2s_d0 from the non-active FIFO in reversed order. Silicon test reports working read/write I2C register access, PWM output, I2C communication with the amplifier, and SPDIF decoding to I2S with good audio, using a clock set to 27 MHz.
